admission.justification: The dated disposition chose one frontend-only repair against a backend/API route and a persistent cache and kept the latency adequacy question open; the choice constrains the reader's data ownership.

alternatives.option: One selection-local records acquisition inside the existing read owner, shared by the toolbar and the Records branch, with old answers cleared on selection changes and no request on rerender, hide/show or Back.
alternatives.reason: The disposition admits exactly this frontend-only repair and removes the demonstrated duplicate acquisition without new state that can go stale.

alternatives.option: Repair the backend route or add a new API for the first-view cost.
alternatives.reason: The disposition admits no backend/API repair; the remaining cost is an owner adequacy question, not a demonstrated backend defect.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The owner judges the remaining first-view cost unacceptable and admits a new backend or API scope.

alternatives.option: Add a persistent or global cache of records answers.
alternatives.reason: The disposition excludes a persistent cache; it would introduce cross-selection state with its own staleness and eviction rules for a saving the selection-local promise already makes.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A measured, owner-admitted need for cross-selection reuse appears.

alternatives.option: Treat about 28 seconds to the first live-leaf document as adequate and close the concern.
alternatives.reason: The samples do not establish adequate speed or a cause; no numeric limit is in the packet, so the adequacy decision stays with the owner.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The owner records an adequacy judgment on the current samples, with or without a numeric limit.

consequences: The toolbar's lookup and the Records branch consume one promise per current selection; expansion adds no request.
A delayed or failed list is named and leaves the document, header and path tree usable.
The first-root latency observation stays with the owner as an adequacy and landing boundary.
context: The exempt takeover returned owner concern L79-TK-O1: the live-leaf reader took tens of seconds to show its first document, and the toolbar and the Records branch independently fetched the same selection's record list. Orchestrator OR-R012 (2026-10-06) had provisionally accepted the material same-source tree-feature cost and set non-gating constraints (header/prose and Back must not wait; no rescan per render; no cache or framework project; material slowdown returns to the Orchestrator). The dated owner disposition L79-TK-O1-OWNER-DISPOSITION-20261007.json (2026-10-07T08:15:37+02:00) then admitted ONE frontend same-selection record-list acquisition repair: existing frontend owners/hooks only, no persistent cache, no new API and no backend repair, with before/after controlled evidence.
decider: Owner disposition of 2026-10-07 (notes/run3/L79-TK-O1-OWNER-DISPOSITION-20261007.json), which admits the frontend repair; OR-R012 (2026-10-06) is retained separately as the background cost/constraint ruling.
